subject: Autoscale / SLO qualification follow-up - FastPay
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Diaz <carlos@fastpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:12:08 -0700
Subject: Autoscale / SLO qualification follow-up - FastPay

Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can size the autoscale + burst recommendations to meet your SLOs:

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Target p95 latency for end-to-end responses (streaming enabled) <= 300ms for 512-token completions
- p99 target <= 700ms (soft) for 512-token completions
- Typical sustained throughput: ~120 QPS; peak bursts up to ~450 QPS for 3–7 minutes during batch payouts
- Concurrent active connections: ~35 normal, up to 220 during peak windows (many are streaming responses)
- Streaming percent: ~60% of requests use streaming (token-by-token client playback)

Key autoscale considerations for SLO adherence we discussed:
- Warm pools: recommended warm pool equivalent to ~20–25% of peak concurrency to avoid cold-start latency on short bursts
- Scale-up time: cold scale-up from zero typically 90–180s depending on instance type; warm pool reduces effective scale-up to ~10–30s
- Queueing policy: short, prioritized queue for latency-sensitive traffic with early reject/fallback to smaller model if queue exceeds threshold
- Burst capacity: ability to temporarily exceed committed capacity for up to 10 minutes with graceful degradation and fallback routing

Requested next steps (proposed):
1) Share a short sample of production traffic (anonymized) or a synthetic load profile with QPS/concurrency over a 24h and 7-day window — this lets us model latency distribution and recommend instance mix.
2) Schedule a 1h technical deep-dive (Neha + Rishi) to validate streaming behavior and warm-pool sizing (propose Tue/Thu afternoons).
3) We'll provide a preliminary Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an autoscale sizing deck + whitepaper (attached) by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood-autoscale-whitepaper.pdf (brief), FP-MAP-autoscale.xlsx (skeleton MAP)

If that all looks right, I can coordinate scheduling and get Rishi to run a quick cost/latency model once we have your sample.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

> Thanks Marissa — great overview today. I forwarded the slides to Elena and product ops.
> Two clarifications: our peak bursts can sometimes hit 600 QPS for up to 2 minutes during settlement windows, and about 10% of requests are long generations (1k+ tokens) — how does that change warm pool sizing?
> —Carlos

From: Carlos Diaz <carlos@fastpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@fastpay.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscale / SLO qualification follow-up - FastPay

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple of follow-ups to help quantify: 

- Confirming numbers: sustained 120 QPS, spikes up to 600 QPS (2–7 minutes), concurrency during spikes ~220–600 depending on client fanout.
- Long generations: ~10% >1k tokens, most of which are non-streaming (batch summaries).
- Streaming behavior: streaming requests are typically low-latency-sensitive (user chat), batch summaries can tolerate higher latency.

Two asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood provide a small telemetry snippet (examples of perf delta between cold start, warm pool warmup, and steady) so we can present to infra?
2) Can we do the deep-dive next Tuesday (Jun 29) at 10am PT? Neha/Rishi OK for that?

Thanks,
Carlos
Director, Platform Engineering | FastPay
carlos@fastpay.com | +1 650-555-0133

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Autoscale / SLO qualification follow-up - FastPay

Carlos — thanks for the extra detail. Confirmed for Tue Jun 29 10:00am PT for the technical deep-dive. Rishi and Neha are looped.

Quick notes before the call so we come prepared:
- Warm pool sizing guidance: with 10% long generations, we should size warm pool by active streaming concurrency and a fraction of long-generation concurrency. For your numbers (220–600 concurrency during peaks), recommended warm pool ~130–160 instances (rough estimate) depending on instance SKU and model latency profile. We'll refine after we see the sample traffic.
- Telemetry snippet: attaching a short perf table in the MAP and will include examples: cold start median ~1.8–3.5s (for large instances), warm pool ramp ~10–30s to full capacity, steady-state p95 <300ms for optimized model and instance mix.
- Fallback policy: propose a canary fallback to smaller quantized model for excess traffic past burst threshold to keep p95 within SLO for latency-sensitive clients.

Action items for you ahead of Tue:
- Share anonymized traffic sample (ideally one full peak window + 24h baseline) to support modeling.
- Add any compliance or security questions you want covered for Private deployment (if you expect regulated flows).

We'll circulate a short MAP before EOD Monday with the items we'll cover in the deep-dive.

Cheers,
Marissa
